source_text: - Hold the subagent session lock and each workspace-writer lock for as long as the owning process runs, instead of leaving a record file that a later process ages out and reclaims. A Jouzu process that exits for any reason, including a kill, releases its locks immediately, so a stopped process no longer blocks a session or leaves a workspace writer queued, while a suspended process keeps its lock. A lock file left behind by an earlier run no longer blocks a new owner, and the five-second recovery grace period is gone. A Jouzu process running a version from before this change does not share these locks, so close other Jouzu processes before upgrading and start them again afterward.

source_text: - Add a built-in `shisa-api` catalog source: when `SHISA_API_KEY` holds a bearer token, Jouzu reads the account's model catalog from the deployed Shisa endpoint with no source configuration, refreshes each enabled source with an available credential in the background at interactive startup, and keeps serving cached catalogs. Without the key and without a configured source, Jouzu makes no catalog request. A manual registration with the same endpoint and credential reference keeps its label, enabled state, and cache; the built-in source can be disabled in Settings / Catalogs without storing a credential.

source_text: Extension selection and confirmation dialogs are relayed through ACP permission requests. Text input and editor dialogs use form elicitation when the host advertises that capability. Without form elicitation, those dialogs are cancelled; hosts that support notices also receive an explanation. While one of these dialogs waits for the user, the prompt acknowledgment timeout is suspended; after the response, a fresh timeout budget applies.

source_text: **ACP is not a sandbox.** Tools run with the same operating-system access as the launched Jouzu process. A working directory does not restrict filesystem access. Relaying extension dialogs does not add approval checks to every tool call. Use trusted workspaces, extensions, and hosts, and launch Jouzu under an account with appropriate access.

source_text: `camoufox-adapter.ts` registers `tff-fetch_url` and `tff-search_web` without installing or importing Camoufox during startup. The first browser tool call runs `npm ci` from `camoufox-runtime/package-lock.json` into a private, versioned directory under Jouzu state, verifies the locked package versions, and dynamically imports the runtime. The same call downloads the Camoufox browser when it is absent. A browser left idle for `JOUZU_CAMOUFOX_IDLE_STOP_MS` (five minutes by default, `0` to keep it loaded) is stopped in the background: the adapter resets its cached runtime promise and delegate map synchronously, closes the client without blocking the next call, and reloads a fresh client on the following call. `session_shutdown` closes a client that was loaded during the session, disarms the idle timer, and drains a stop that is still in flight within a grace period.

A provider supporting streaming does not establish that these conditions hold. Models with zero configured prices do not warm automatically; extensions can override that cost-based decision.

source_text: The `windows-npm-*` artifacts contain npm timing/debug logs and the selected paths. `windows-defender-*` records protection state and exclusion cleanup. If an image with protection disabled stops answering Defender queries and the job added no exclusions, cleanup records `not-required` with unknown final state and the query error. Other query failures fail the job. Compare elapsed time from the first Windows job start to the last Windows job finish, and inspect the artifact producer's duration separately. Adding parallel job durations measures runner usage, not elapsed time.

source_text: Source compatibility jobs use `node scripts/install-source-dependencies.mjs` followed by `JOUZU_BUILD_SOURCE_ONLY=1 npm run build`. source_text: Jouzu preserves native clipboard copying and also sends copied text to tmux's paste buffer. It asks tmux to forward the text to a terminal client attached to the current pane's session. This works with tmux's default `set-clipboard external`; you do not need to set `set-clipboard on`. Jouzu does not change your tmux configuration.

source_text: When standard input closes, Jouzu resolves unanswered dialogs with their defaults and gives accepted commands up to five seconds to answer. A command still unanswered after that reports one failure. Cleanup then gets up to five seconds of its own; if it cannot finish, Jouzu reports one `shutdown` failure and exits with status 1. Responses and diagnostics already written are flushed first.

source_text: A shutdown failure from an extension request or a signal reports the same way: one `shutdown` failure, one flush, status 1. A second ordinary shutdown request waits for the one in progress instead of exiting early, so queued output is not lost and a failing status is not replaced by success. A shutdown requested after input has ended also waits for the command drain, so every accepted command still reports before the process exits. `SIGTERM` and `SIGHUP` keep their own exit status and exit at once when a shutdown is already in progress. Keep standard input open for commands that can take longer than five seconds.

source_text: - At the session-input boundary, a command runs locally only when the message starts with its name followed by a space or the end of the message; everything after the first space is the command's argument. Other text, such as `/flow` followed by a tab, `/flows`, an unknown name, or a prompt sent with template expansion off, is a message: flow control holds or delivers it like any other input. The interactive editor trims surrounding whitespace and accepts a full-width slash before dispatch, so leading spaces do not quote an interactive command. RPC input is not trimmed; external adapter input is always literal.

Producer tools and their own delivery paths keep working while it is off, and `/flow runtime` still reports the running and installed versions.

source_text: When `SHISA_API_KEY` holds a bearer token, the built-in `shisa-api` source reads the account's model catalog from `https://api.shisa.ai/v1/jouzu/model-catalog` without any source configuration. Interactive startup refreshes each enabled source whose credential is available, in the background, while cached catalogs keep serving. Without the key and without a configured source, Jouzu makes no catalog request. The token is sent only as the source's authorization header, is never written to configuration, cache, or diagnostics, and authenticated refresh never follows redirects.

source_text: Settings / Catalogs (`/catalogs`) manages named sources: add, edit, enable/disable, refresh, and remove, with per-source ETag validation, account-partitioned cache, mass-change quarantine, and last-known-good retention. The built-in source can be disabled there without storing a credential; a manual registration with the same endpoint and credential reference keeps its label, enabled state, and cache. `jouzu catalog status|refresh [source-id]` and `jouzu catalog accept REVISION --digest SHA256 --source SOURCE_ID` provide CLI parity. `JOUZU_MODEL_CATALOG_URL` and `JOUZU_MODEL_CATALOG_TOKEN` remain a single-source shorthand when `catalogs.json` is absent.

source_text: Use `/voice` to start microphone dictation and `/voice stop` to insert the transcript into the prompt. `Ctrl+\` starts or stops recording from the prompt; set `jouzu.voice.toggle` to change or remove the binding. source_text: `npm run test:affected` compares the working tree and untracked files with `HEAD` (or `--base REF`) and runs the Node test files that import a changed file, directly or through other sources and test fixtures. Compiled imports under `dist/` map to their `src/` files, and tests that launch the built CLI count as importing it. A changed workflow, manifest, or document selects the tests that name it. Changes to dependencies, build scripts, `upstream/`, or shared script fixtures select every test file. It skips `@endurance` tests unless you pass `--endurance`, and it refuses to run CLI tests against a stale build. Pass paths to select tests for specific files, and run `node scripts/affected-tests.mjs` without `--run` to list the selection.

source_text: Tests whose names end in `@endurance` repeat full runtime operations until they cross a production storage limit, such as 1,120 tool turns past the native request quota. The default CLI suite (`npm run test --workspace packages/cli`) skips them; `npm run test:endurance --workspace packages/cli` runs only them. `npm test` runs `test:full`, the whole CLI suite including endurance tests, so they share the suite's parallel workers. Tag a new test `@endurance` only when it must cross an exact production limit, and list its file in the `test:endurance` script. `scripts/gate-commands.test.mjs` fails when the list and the tagged files differ.

source_text: The budget compares each test's median with its tier. Each CI job contributes one sample, so failure limits leave room for a runner stall (a 0.07-second test once took 4 seconds); warnings report smaller growth. CI checks the Ubuntu/Node 22 CLI suite and the endurance job: a test over its failure budget fails pushes and manual runs and warns on pull requests. A new test that needs more than its tier allows must state the guarantee it adds and be assigned a tier in the manifest; prefer making it faster.

source_text: `schedule_prompt` with `action: "add"` returns a `waitDependency` when flow control is on. source_text: Work labels associate a wait with a task or session; they do not grant permission to use a dependency. Omit `agent_wait.work` or set it to `null` to use the current task or session. A paused task keeps its wait association so resuming does not duplicate the wait and stopping the task cancels it. An exact live `replaceToken` can replace a wait after task attribution changes, but cannot displace a separate live wait on the destination task. Missing or stale attribution must not prevent a valid tool call. Dependencies still require exact producer, handle, and execution identities so a wait cannot observe the wrong job. Pi's strict-schema converter does not support nullable objects; `strict: "prefer"` falls back to the registered non-strict schema without dropping nullability.

source_text: Replace the path with the extension's absolute entry-file path. Grants match its canonical filesystem identity and adapter ID. Relative paths, globs, duplicate grants, and unknown fields are rejected. A missing file denies registration. The file must be a regular file, not a symlink, and at most 64 KiB. Rechecks must match the canonical extension identity captured at registration; redirecting an entry-file symlink cannot transfer an existing handle or its retained messages to another granted extension.

source_text: A live runtime holds one registration per canonical extension identity and adapter ID. Registering that identity again while the first registration is live fails with `adapter-already-registered`, and the first registration, its target listeners, and its published target stay unchanged, so register once per runtime and reuse the returned handle. `adapter-already-registered` describes registration identity; it is not the message-level `id-conflict`. After an extension reload the replaced runtime's handles are inert and its registration is gone, so the replacement runtime registers the same identity normally.

source_text: An administrative flow reset starts a new target epoch. The host reports it through `adapter.onTargetInvalidated`, and every listener must withdraw the published target, call `bind()` again, and publish the new one. Messages composed against the withdrawn target are never retargeted; each needs a fresh human action for the new target. Feature-detect `onTargetInvalidated` if the extension also runs on hosts that do not report it. Reset also fences admission: a submission that validated the previous target either settles before the reset or is refused with `stale-target`, and a prepared dispatch is refused at execution instead of delivering into the new journal lifetime.

source_text: Submission returns after durable admission, without waiting for the provider to finish. Reuse the original message ID and payload when recovering a receipt. Changed text or delivery mode under the same ID is an `id-conflict`. Consumed, queued, and uncertain dispatches are never resent. Only a callback that ended before any dispatch intent can be reattached by an authorized retry for the same stable target. The host rechecks the grant and the target immediately before entering native input handling, including when a send waits for the settled event. A grant revoked or a target rotated before that check refuses the dispatch; its receipt stays `unknown` and the message is not replayed. Revocation does not cancel input that has already entered native handling, including input waiting in an asynchronous input handler. It is not an interrupt for an in-flight instruction.

source_text: Subscriptions publish an initial snapshot, including archived messages, followed by updates for messages whose stored evidence changed. Unrelated journal writes do not republish unchanged receipts. Each update pass still scans active records and archived index metadata, but reads archived payloads only when their evidence changed. Updates carry `version: 1`, adapter/message identity, target, journal generation and revision, state, and an optional structured reason. Notifications are hints; use lookup after reconnect. Listener failures do not change delivery. A failed authorization or snapshot pass is reported through the host's error channel and resumes only on a later journal write; repairing the fault alone does not trigger another pass. After a reported fault, use `lookup` to recover current receipts and unsubscribe and subscribe again to request a fresh snapshot. Unsubscribe on shutdown and subscribe again after branch navigation.

source_text: New message IDs are limited to 16,384 and 64 MiB of encoded admission payload per branch journal lifetime, across adapters and including archived records. Active records also share the submission store's 1,024-record/4 MiB admission budget. Receipt evidence has a separate bound; new-ID exhaustion does not prevent lookup, safe reattachment, or normal evidence updates. Payload and deduplication evidence remain for that journal lifetime; draining or archiving does not reclaim the budget. Administrative flow-state reset starts a new journal lifetime and budget, invalidating the target and the deduplication guarantee. Reset is not routine capacity cleanup: withdraw the published target, bind again, and accept new messages only for the new target.

source_text: Turning flow control off rejects submissions with `flow-suspended` and cancels external input that has not acquired dispatch intent. Registration and authorized lookup remain available. Already queued or running input retains its native evidence; it is not retroactively declared undelivered. An unreadable or malformed grants file (`invalid-config`) is a repairable fault, not a revocation: retained and queued input is held and becomes admissible on a later release or queue-admission pass after the file is repaired. If the host drops a queued entry without taking it, the receipt advances to `unknown` at a new journal revision, so subscriptions and lookup correct a stored `queued` receipt.

source_text: Branch navigation pauses admission while the host settles the old attachment. New submissions in that interval are refused with `flow-suspended` or `stale-target`. A retention already in progress is cancelled without dispatch if it crosses that boundary. Input already retained without dispatch does not prevent navigation: it remains in the departing branch's journal, without automatic replay. Returning to that branch restores its stable target but requires a fresh binding; the ended callback can be reattached only by an authorized explicit retry.

source_text: Session replacement instead disposes the outgoing attachment and retires its adapter handles; it can proceed with held external input. Undispatched input remains in the outgoing journal and is not replayed. On reopening that journal, its receipt reports `unknown` with reason `callback-ended`; an authorized explicit retry can reattach it only if no dispatch intent exists. A new session has a different target, not permission to resend the old message.

source_text: 1. **Every action must be reachable without a modified key.** Modified keys are accelerators. `Ctrl`, `Alt`, `Shift`, and `Super` combinations that a legacy terminal cannot encode are unavailable to some users on every platform; see [Encoding and line discipline](key-collisions.md#encoding-and-line-discipline). A recorded decision may accept an accelerator-only action; the current exception is Models favorite (`jouzu.model.toggleFavorite`), recorded in [Palette primary and secondary actions](palette-ux.md#primary-and-secondary-actions).

source_text: 2. **Check the complete binding definitions before claiming a key.** Review Pi's `KEYBINDINGS` (TUI actions, application actions, and platform overrides), Jouzu's `JOUZU_KEYBINDING_DEFINITIONS` in `jouzu-keybindings.ts`, and the seeded overrides in `JOUZU_KEYBINDING_DEFAULTS`. Check the effective user bindings for the affected view as well. A raw `matchesKey` call that shadows an action eligible in the same scope is a defect.

source_text: 4. **A mode with a live text field has no bare-letter and no bare-`Space` shortcuts.** While a text field holds focus, letters, digits, punctuation, and `Space` belong to it. A mode with no text field may use them. This protects search and IME composition; see [Text, language, and input](#text-language-and-input). A view with type-to-search, where typing focuses the search field, has no usable bare-letter layer even in browse; its browse actions use non-printable unmodified keys only.
